messages.author: c14d23408a6f22dd
messages.subject: Log scale x-axis woes
parts:
Dear list members,

I'm hopng someone might offer some suggestions or confirm this odd
behaviour I have observed when plotting log-scale x-axis plots with
ggplot2. The link below illustrates the issue better than I could
likely explain it:

http://also.imgur.com/log_scale_xaxis_woes

Notice that when using the regular plot() function, my plot for
neutrophils dips down abruptly near the y-axis and ends. In contrast,
the ggplot2 version dips in a similar fashion, then rebounds then dips
again. I included a more extreme example (for which I, unfortunately,
do not have a plot() counter-example on my local machine) labelled
"Basophils (ggplot2)".

Is there anyway to ensure that this sort of behaviour does not happen?
Any help is appreciated!

Thanks,

Casey

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Log scale x-axis woes
parts:
Hi:

I'm guessing this phenomenon has something to do with the interaction of your data and the geom used to produce the plot, but since you've supplied neither, it's difficult to supply concrete advice to what is currently an abstract problem :) Please provide a small example (data + code) that illustrates the problem and what you expect, and you might have better luck in obtaining a solution. For example, I could see this happening if you had multiple, consecutive observations at the same x while using geom_path(), but that's speculation. Facts are better...

Dennis
